name: signature_vulnerabilities
description: Insecure signature verification enabling replay, malleability, or zero-address forgery attacks
question: The source file in `source` contains a function that uses `ecrecover` or an ECDSA `recover` call to authenticate or authorize a user action (e.g. permit, meta-transaction, gasless approval), and it fails to prevent signature reuse or forgery because it omits at least one of: a per-user nonce that is checked and incremented before executing the action, a chain ID or verifying-contract-bound domain separator (EIP-712) protecting against cross-chain/cross-contract replay, or an explicit check that the recovered signer is not `address(0)`, thereby allowing an attacker to replay, reuse, or forge a valid-looking signature to execute unauthorized actions.
criteria: ecrecover(...) or ECDSA.recover(...) result is used to authorize an action without checking `recovered != address(0)`
Signed message hash is built with keccak256(abi.encodePacked(...)) omitting chain ID and/or verifying contract address (no EIP-712 domain separator), enabling cross-chain or cross-contract replay
Signature-based function lacks a nonce mapping (or bitmap) that is checked and marked used, allowing the same signature to be submitted repeatedly (same-contract replay)
Domain separator is computed once at construction using block.chainid without being recomputed on fork/chain-change detection
Signature verification accepts arbitrary s values with no low-s / malleability check and does not use OpenZeppelin's ECDSA library
Recovered signer is compared to expected signer only via require(signer == expectedSigner) with no prior zero-address guard
